A bicycle gear system allows riders to adjust the resistance and speed of pedaling, making it easier to ride uphill or faster on flat terrain. It works by changing the ratio between the front chainrings (attached to the pedals) and the rear sprockets (attached to the rear wheel). This ratio determines how many times the rear wheel turns for each pedal revolution.

Most bikes have multiple chainrings on the front and several sprockets on the rear. When you shift gears, a derailleur moves the chain between these different-sized rings and sprockets. For example, using a large front chainring with a small rear sprocket creates a high gear ratio, meaning each pedal stroke turns the rear wheel many times—ideal for fast, flat rides.
